facts.claim: The list subcommand currently accepts only --priority and --due options; no --json option exists.
The existing list path loads the configured store, applies the priority and due filters, sorts the filtered tasks, prints one human-readable row per task, and returns exit code 0.
Human-readable list rows are tab-separated and contain id, status ([ ] or [x]), priority, due date (or -), and title in that order.
Tests lock the exact existing human-readable output for a task as `1\t[ ]\thigh\t-\talpha\n`.
Listing an empty or missing store currently emits no stdout or stderr, exits 0, and does not create the store file.
Each task record has exactly five modeled fields: id (integer), title (string), done (boolean), due (string or null), and priority (string).
The existing task-to-dictionary serialization uses keys id, title, done, due, and priority and preserves their native JSON-compatible types.
List filtering is exact-match filtering by priority and/or due date, with both filters applied when both are supplied.
Tests require combined priority and due filters to restrict list results to records matching both conditions.
List sorting orders incomplete tasks before completed tasks, then higher priority first, then earlier due dates with null due dates last, then lower task id.
Tests lock the list sort order, including incomplete-before-done, high-before-medium-before-low, dated-before-undated within equal status and priority, and id as the final tiebreaker.
The README documents list as producing the current text rows, supporting exact-match combinable filters, producing no output for an empty list, and applying sorting after filtering.
Invalid list due-date syntax is handled by argument parsing and returns usage exit code 2.
Store and domain failures are printed to stderr as `error: ...` and return exit codes 3 and 1 respectively; successful list execution returns 0.
Listing a corrupt store returns exit code 3 and leaves the store byte-for-byte unchanged.
The CLI uses only the Python standard library at runtime and declares no runtime dependencies.
